Public specification:
Build a 32-bit global history shift register, including support for rolling back state in response to a pipeline flush caused by a branch misprediction. When a branch prediction is made (predict_valid = 1), shift in predict_taken from the LSB side to update the branch history for the predicted branch. (predict_history[0] is the direction of the youngest branch.) When a branch misprediction occurs (train_mispredicted = 1), load the branch history register with the history after the completion of the mispredicted branch. This is the history before the mispredicted branch (train_history) concatenated with the actual result of the branch (train_taken). If both a prediction and misprediction occur at the same time, the misprediction takes precedence, because the pipeline flush will also flush out the branch that is currently making a prediction. predict_history is the value of the branch history register. areset is a positive edge triggered asynchronous reset that resets the history counter to zero.



Input widths {'areset': 1, 'predict_valid': 1, 'predict_taken': 1, 'train_mispredicted': 1, 'train_taken': 1, 'train_history': 32}; output widths {'predict_history': 32}. Clock clk; sample after the posedge edge has settled. Each row's values are driven before the sampled edge. Optional mid input changes occur AFTER sampling, before the other edge, and are carried to the start of the next row. Protocol seed 20261124.
Write a rigorous JSON behavior contract, not executable code. Use these keys:
ports {inputs:{name:width},outputs:{name:width},clock:name or null}.
states [{name,meaning,update_time,update_during_reset:boolean}].
rules [{id,outputs:[names],condition,edge:"posedge"|"negedge"|"combinational"|"asynchronous",
visible:"same_cycle"|"next_cycle",priority:integer,spec_quote,uncertain:boolean,
example:{vectors:[input rows],expected:[output rows]}}].
Every output must appear in some rule. Each rule has one example of 2–4 cycles. Vectors contain every
nonclock input with a width-valid unsigned integer and may contain "mid" with changed inputs.
Expected contains each rule output on EVERY row (all outputs are allowed). Use unsigned integers.
A spec_quote is a short verbatim substring of the supplied spec. If missing or ungrounded it MUST be
marked uncertain, and the uncertain list MUST have an entry for that rule. An interface or protocol timing
sentence is not design evidence. For a waveform-only task use a verbatim printed row or mark the inference uncertain.
reset {kind:"none"|"sync"|"async"|"unspecified",name:input or null,active:"high"|"low"|"none"|"unspecified",
values:{output:value or null},first_released_cycle:string}.
mid:string. uncertain [{rule_id,note,candidates:[distinct interpretation strings]}].
Keep any deliberation brief and prioritize a complete compact JSON object. Keep independent rules
concise and do not invent specification text.
